name: Ransomware attack in four phases
about: The challenge scenario: the budget, 22 controls from the original control-card deck, and four attack phases. Players choose all their controls once, before the attack starts. Aggregate control totals from the deck are preserved across the phases.

setting.boundary: No live grid, real customer data or actual company infrastructure

learning_objectives: Explain prevention, detection and response as complementary layers
Support a colleague who reports a mistake
Verify unexpected requests through a trusted independent route
Apply a principle to an unfamiliar situation

controls.name: Anti Malware
controls.description: Scans the company's network to identify and remove malicious software.
controls.use_case: Helps detect and remove malware on systems covered by the Prevent purchase.
controls.limitation: It cannot guarantee detection of every malicious program.

controls.name: Network segmentation
controls.description: Divides a large network into smaller groups with controlled connections.
controls.use_case: Can slow malware spread and restrict an attacker's movement across the network.
controls.limitation: It does not remove malware from an already compromised device.

controls.name: Firewall and DDoS protection
controls.description: Blocks suspicious access and reduces the impact of denial-of-service attacks.
controls.use_case: Filters suspicious traffic at the network boundary and limits some DDoS activity.
controls.limitation: It cannot stop every attack, especially threats arriving through trusted channels.

controls.name: Software patching and updates
controls.description: Applies software changes that fix, update or improve programs and devices.
controls.use_case: Closes known security weaknesses in covered applications and devices.
controls.limitation: Patching does not fix unknown weaknesses or systems outside its coverage.

controls.name: Secure by design
controls.description: Builds security into each level of application, system and network design.
controls.use_case: Reduces avoidable weaknesses before systems are deployed.
controls.limitation: Secure design reduces risk but cannot guarantee that a system is vulnerability-free.

controls.name: Training and awareness program
controls.description: Teaches employees what threats look like, how they work and how to respond.
controls.use_case: Helps staff recognise and report suspicious activity.
controls.limitation: Training cannot prevent every mistake or replace technical controls.

controls.name: Email security
controls.description: Filters suspicious email and lets employees report messages they do not trust.
controls.use_case: Reduces the number of malicious messages reaching employee inboxes.
controls.limitation: Some malicious or convincing messages may still reach users.

controls.name: Network behaviour analysis (NBA)
controls.description: Monitors network traffic and activity for unusual or suspicious behaviour.
controls.use_case: Raises an alert when activity on the network looks unusual.
controls.limitation: An alert requires investigation and does not itself stop the activity.

controls.name: Endpoint detection and response (EDR)
controls.description: Continuously monitors devices for suspicious activity and sends alerts.
controls.use_case: Helps teams identify and address endpoint threats quickly.
controls.limitation: Coverage is limited to the Prevent purchase; alerts still need a response.

controls.name: Security incident and event management (SIEM)
controls.description: Shows activity from people inside and outside the network across applications and devices.
controls.use_case: Helps a monitoring team spot and investigate security incidents across systems.
controls.limitation: The information still needs skilled people to interpret and act on it.

controls.name: Intrusion detection and prevention systems
controls.description: Analyses network activity for malicious behaviour and acts to stop detected incidents.
controls.use_case: Can identify and block some malicious network activity.
controls.limitation: It may miss new or disguised attacks and cannot replace incident response.

controls.name: Vulnerability scanning
controls.description: Scans an organisation's network to find known weaknesses.
controls.use_case: Helps teams identify vulnerabilities that need investigation and remediation.
controls.limitation: A scan finds weaknesses but does not fix them or prove the network is secure.

controls.name: Penetration testing
controls.description: Uses an authorised simulated cyberattack to evaluate system security.
controls.use_case: Finds weaknesses by testing how a system responds to realistic attack techniques.
controls.limitation: It is a point-in-time assessment, not continuous monitoring.

controls.name: Threat hunting and honeypot
controls.description: Searches for signs of attackers and uses decoys to observe suspicious activity.
controls.use_case: Can reveal threats that routine alerts have not detected.
controls.limitation: Hunting and decoys cannot prove that no attacker is present.

controls.name: Endpoint detection and response (EDR)
controls.description: Continuously monitors devices for suspicious activity and sends alerts.
controls.use_case: Helps the Detect team identify and respond to endpoint threats quickly.
controls.limitation: Coverage is limited to the Detect purchase; alerts still need a response.

controls.name: Anti Malware
controls.description: Scans the company's network to identify and remove malicious software.
controls.use_case: Helps the Detect team find malware on covered systems.
controls.limitation: It cannot guarantee detection of every malicious program.

controls.name: Incident response plan
controls.description: Defines roles, decisions and escalation routes before anything goes wrong.
controls.use_case: Useful in every phase, because someone always has to decide who does what.
controls.limitation: Having a plan is different from having practised it.

controls.name: Incident response team - 24/7
controls.description: Provides response capability around the clock.
controls.use_case: Much of this attack happens overnight, when an office-hours team is not available.
controls.limitation: Availability does not mean instant resolution, and by the recovery phase the work has shifted to restoring systems.

controls.name: Incident response team - office hours
controls.description: Provides response capability Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00.
controls.use_case: Cheaper. Covers the working day, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00.
controls.limitation: Out-of-hours coverage has to be arranged some other way.

controls.name: Backup restores
controls.description: Copies backup data from secondary storage back to its original or a new location.
controls.use_case: Helps restore computers, programs and data after an incident.
controls.limitation: Recovery depends on having usable backups that were not also compromised.

controls.name: Incident response retainer
controls.description: Provides access to security expertise through a response partner.
controls.use_case: Helps an organisation respond quickly when a cyber incident occurs.
controls.limitation: A retainer provides support, not an instant resolution.

controls.name: Digital forensics services
controls.description: Examines devices after an incident to determine what happened and how.
controls.use_case: Can identify whether an action was deliberate, how malware arrived and what it did.
controls.limitation: Forensic findings depend on evidence that was preserved and available.

phases.title: Delivery and exploitation
phases.story: Monday, 16:40. Near the end of the working day, an employee opens a trusted-looking message and malicious software reaches their laptop. This rehearsal assumes the attacker gets in. The question is how well your defences and your people limit the damage.

phases.title: Discovery
phases.story: Tuesday, 02:00. While almost nobody is watching, the attacker quietly explores the business's systems. Your team needs useful reports and technical evidence to understand what is happening.

phases.title: Command and control
phases.story: Tuesday, 03:30. The attacker now controls the infected laptop remotely. A caller claiming to be from IT rings the night-shift work-order desk. The team must check the request through a trusted route and coordinate what it does.

phases.title: Encryption and ransom demand
phases.story: Tuesday, 06:30. Just before the day shift starts, business files are encrypted and a ransom demand appears. Practise recovery, clear communication and an honest debrief. The game does not advise on paying a ransom or give real incident instructions.
